passages.title: The shark on the highway
passages.text: Last spring, a photo of a shark swimming along a flooded highway went viral. Within hours it had been shared more than a million times, and several news websites used it under dramatic headlines. The photo looked real, but a few readers noticed something strange: the shark's shadow was in the wrong place. A team of journalists decided to fact-check it. They searched for the original images and found that the shark came from a nature magazine published years earlier. "Someone must have put the two pictures together," they concluded. The person who made it was never found. It might have been a joke that got out of control, or someone might have wanted to bring visitors to a website. Experts say that misleading stories spread faster than true ones, because they surprise us and make us feel strong emotions. Their advice is simple: before you share something, check the source, look for the same story on other websites and ask yourself why someone wants you to see it.

points: Para deducir algo del pasado: modal + «have» + participio.
«must have done» (seguro que sí), «might have done» (quizás), «can't have done» (imposible).
«spread» es difundir(se); su pasado y su participio no cambian: «spread».

examples.en: Someone must have edited the photo.
examples.es: Alguien debe de haber editado la foto.

examples.en: She can't have written it herself.
examples.es: Es imposible que lo haya escrito ella misma.

mistake.note: Para decir que es imposible que algo pasara, usa «can't have», no «mustn't have».

points: «turn out» es resultar: «The rumor turned out to be false», «It turned out that…».
«rule out» es descartar: «We can't rule out an accident»; con pronombre: «rule it out».
«source» es la fuente de una información; «fact-check» es verificar los datos.

examples.en: It turned out that I was right.
The journalists fact-checked the story before publishing it.
examples.es: Los periodistas verificaron la noticia antes de publicarla.

mistake.right: The rumor turned out to be false.
mistake.note: “Resultar” + adjetivo no se dice con «result»: usa «turn out to be».
